main_text.head: PAVLI MELISSI SCHEDII, Ad Theodorum Bezam, ODE.

p.i: ANGVINEOS inter, BEZA, tot hostiū Enses, & iras, quas acuit furor Crudelis infesta Megera, Et rabies truculenta Martis, Tu ne etiam nostri non reminiscier Ne quis, & imo pectore pro tuo Preces MELISSO fospitales Fundere, & haud peritura vota, Dictaque caelestes omnibus pijs Tangentia auras? Dia superstitet, Contra precabor, te Salutis Ala, nouans viridem senectam More aquilae, donec qua Deus optimus Bona immerenti grandia desuper Conferre gratis destinauit, Conferat, & benefacta largis Multiplicet donis. Spondeo, nam quidem Tauros, & aras munera victimas, Aut pingue ferclum[?], sed pudicam Mentem animi, memoremq; linguam M. iuj.[?]

page.notes: The decorated initial A of ANGVINEOS is a large ornamental letter. Small capitals in the poem: BEZA, MELISSO. Doubtful readings: "ferclum" in line 19 is unclear (possibly a Latin word for a ceremonial dish); the closing signature "M. iuj." is hard to read and may be an abbreviated name. The tilde over "hostiū" is copied as printed. The printed "fospitales" and "Dia superstitet" are copied as printed.
